title: Ferrari reveals special F1 car livery for Monza celebrating Michael Schumacher’s legacy
content:
Ferrari will celebrate Michael Schumacher’s legacy with a special, one-off Formula 1 car livery for this weekend’s Italian Grand Prix at Monza.

Ferrari revealed its revised paint scheme for its home race weekend on Tuesday, as well as providing more details on events to celebrate 30 years since Schumacher joined the team.

Schumacher won five of his seven world championships while racing for Ferrari between 1996 and 2006, becoming the most successful driver in its history. In his first season with the team, he scored its first Italian GP win at Monza since 1988.

In honor of Schumacher, Ferrari will adopt a livery inspired by its 1996 car design for this weekend, featuring retro car numbers, white wings, plus a red engine cover and cockpit to replace the usual white.

Both Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton’s cars will also carry Schumacher’s personal logo, as well as seven white stars — one for each of his championships — on the nose of the car. The drivers will also have special race suits, gloves and shoes for this weekend.

Ferrari will also celebrate Schumacher by putting three of his cars on display at Monza. The model from his first season in 1996, the Ferrari F310, will be joined by Schumacher’s final Ferrari from 2006, the 248 F1, and the F2002 which provided the German with one of his greatest F1 campaigns.

Schumacher’s teammate from the 2002 season, Rubens Barrichello, will take part in a show run behind the wheel of the F2002 car on Saturday at Monza. Barrichello raced alongside Schumacher in all five of his title-winning years for Ferrari, and scored victory at Monza in the 2002 car.

Another ex-Ferrari driver, Sebastian Vettel, will then get behind the wheel of the F2002 for a demonstration lap on Sunday ahead of the race. Vettel drove for Ferrari between 2015 and 2020, and regarded Schumacher as one of his racing heroes.

After initially retiring from F1 at the end of the 2006 season, Schumacher had planned to return to Ferrari in 2009 as a mid-season replacement for the injured Felipe Massa, only for an issue with his neck to prevent a reunion with the Italian team.

Schumacher returned to full-time racing in 2010 with Mercedes before making his final grand prix start at the end of the 2012 season.

His tally of seven world championships has since been matched by Hamilton, who joined Ferrari at the start of 2025. The Briton is the only driver in F1 history to surpass Schumacher’s total of 91 grand prix victories.

Schumacher has not been seen publicly since sustaining severe head injuries in a skiing accident in December 2013, with his family maintaining strict privacy around his medical condition.

His son, Mick Schumacher, became Formula 2 champion in 2020 and spent two seasons racing in F1 for Haas. He subsequently moved into sports car racing and, since 2026, has driven in IndyCar in the United States.
